name: Photochemistry
tagline: Light-driven reactions, photocatalysis, and solar energy conversion.
seo_title: Photochemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Photochemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in photocatalysis, solar fuels, photophysics and light-driven synthesis.

definition.lead: Photochemistry studies reactions started by light: a molecule absorbs a photon, reaches an excited state and does chemistry that is impossible in the dark.
definition.body: Light drives photosynthesis, vision, vitamin D formation and the ozone layer. In the lab, light lets chemists build strained rings, activate stable bonds at room temperature and turn sunlight into fuels and electricity.

timeline.title: Plants need light
timeline.text: Jan Ingenhousz shows that plants restore air only in sunlight.
timeline.why: The discovery of photosynthesis's dependence on light.

timeline.title: Only absorbed light acts
timeline.text: Theodor von Grotthuss states that only absorbed light can drive a chemical change.

timeline.title: The photochemistry of the future
timeline.text: Giacomo Ciamician imagines industry powered by sunlight instead of coal.
timeline.why: A vision now pursued by solar-fuel research.

timeline.title: The ozone cycle
timeline.text: Sydney Chapman explains how UV light forms and destroys stratospheric ozone.

timeline.title: Flash photolysis
timeline.text: Ronald Norrish and George Porter use intense flashes to create and study short-lived species.
timeline.why: Opened fast photochemistry; Nobel Prize in 1967.

timeline.title: The path of carbon
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Melvin Calvin for the carbon assimilation cycle in photosynthesis.
timeline.why: Explained how plants turn CO₂ into sugar.

timeline.title: Water split with light
timeline.text: Akira Fujishima and Kenichi Honda use titanium dioxide and light to split water.

timeline.title: The dye-sensitized solar cell
timeline.text: Brian O'Regan and Michael Grätzel report an efficient dye-sensitized cell.
timeline.why: A new, low-cost kind of solar cell.

timeline.title: Ozone depletion
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Crutzen, Molina and Rowland for atmospheric chemistry of ozone.
timeline.why: Led to the global phase-out of ozone-destroying chemicals.

timeline.title: Visible-light photoredox
timeline.text: Groups including David MacMillan's bring photoredox catalysis to organic synthesis.
timeline.why: Light became a routine reagent in synthesis labs.

quiz.q: What does the first law of photochemistry say?
options: Only absorbed light can cause a photochemical change
Heat is a form of light
quiz.explain: Light that passes straight through does nothing chemically.

quiz.q: Why does phosphorescence last longer than fluorescence?
options: It comes from a spin-forbidden transition out of a triplet state
The excited molecule is hotter and cools slowly
It only happens in molecules with heavy atoms
It is a slow chemical reaction, not light emission
quiz.explain: Spin-forbidden transitions are slow, so the glow lingers.

quiz.q: As wavelength decreases, the energy of a photon…
quiz.explain: E = hc/λ: UV photons carry more energy than red ones.
Two alkenes join into a four-membered ring.

quiz.q: Why do many [2+2] cycloadditions need light?
options: Orbital symmetry forbids them thermally but allows them from the excited state
Light simply heats the flask to start the reaction
Light acts only as a catalyst that is regenerated
Light adds mass to the molecules so they react
quiz.explain: Exciting an electron changes which orbitals overlap.

quiz.q: Stratospheric ozone forms when UV light…
options: Splits O₂ into oxygen atoms that then join O₂
Splits water vapour into hydrogen and oxygen
Turns carbon dioxide into ozone directly
quiz.explain: O + O₂ → O₃, the Chapman mechanism.

quiz.q: What did Fujishima and Honda do with TiO₂ and light in 1972?
quiz.explain: The first well-known semiconductor photoelectrode for water splitting.

options: Absorb visible light and transfer single electrons
Absorb X-rays and break bonds directly
Heat the reaction mixture like a hot plate
Release oxygen that oxidizes the substrate
quiz.explain: The excited catalyst becomes a strong oxidant or reductant.

quiz.q: Which pigment captures light in plants?
quiz.explain: It absorbs mainly red and blue light, so plants look green.
A dye absorbs light and injects electrons into titanium dioxide.

quiz.q: Vitamin D forms in skin when UVB light…
options: Splits water in the skin cells
Heats the blood near the surface
quiz.explain: The ring-opened product then rearranges into vitamin D₃.

quiz.q: Who gave the 1912 lecture 'The Photochemistry of the Future'?
quiz.explain: He pictured glass-covered fields making chemicals from sunlight.
